posts.headline: Forty-six editions deep and Thicks finally handed me a gift — Klint's Clipboard is still 6-2 and 934.5 points-for, but that's two straight editions of flatlined scoring while the ring collects dust.
posts.detail: A title with a 14-14 career record and a 5.5 average finish was always borrowed pedigree, and freezing at 934.5 points for two days running doesn't look like a champion hitting his stride — it looks like a fraud running out the clock.

posts.headline: Shake N Bakers are no longer a sleeper story, they're just the best team in Busters Anonymous, full stop.
posts.detail: triciagloston's 1128.92 points-for leads the league outright at 6-2, a wild leap from a career 6-7-1 mark and a 5th-place average finish — the quiet dominance arc has officially graduated to loud supremacy.

posts.headline: One Nut Barner's collapse is now the defining storyline of the season — a 1.5 career average finish sinking to 2-6.
posts.detail: Put it in Ra's 20-8 career record and back-to-back championship-game appearances mean nothing when 874.16 points-for can't even crack .500, proving that pedigree without production is just a nice résumé on a losing team.

posts.headline: Sasinci can't escape 4-4 and Big Head's title defense is now a full-blown cold case.
posts.detail: A former champion sitting at 905.74 points-for, second-lowest among .500-or-better teams, is exactly the kind of underwhelming stretch that makes you wonder if Megamind's next threat to quit the league might finally be the real one.

posts.headline: BIBLE OR THE BELT is still winless at 0-8 and Eli's Ultimate Light Skin has turned this season into a full Old Testament plague cycle.
posts.detail: 874.99 points-for isn't even the problem — a career 13-14-1 record says this team should be hovering around mediocrity, but 0-8 means the Belt has been chosen again, and again, and again.
